messages:
oncall_jordan: PAGED: p99 latency spike noticed across us-west-1 inference pool, streaming stalls reported by multiple customers. Paging SRE. Seeing SLO breaches on /v1/generate p95 and p99.
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency_high_us-west-1 triggered at 2026-03-15T09:14:48Z severity=critical -> paging oncall_jordan.
sre_ana: acknowledged — joining. any obvious deploys or config changes?
oncall_jordan: nothing in deploy history in last 30m. error rates ~stable but tail latency up. dashboards: p95 ~1.1s -> 2.8s, p99 spiking to 6-8s. streaming stalls (clients see CRs with no tokens for 4-6s).
infra_lee: running quick check on kv-cache stats. can someone grab kvcachectl metrics for us-west-1?
eng_evans: grabbing now, `kvcachectl metrics --region us-west-1 --prefix kv-prefill` -> returning evictions/sec: 1850, occupancy: 92%, fragment_count: 11, decode_queue_len_avg: 18. prefill_rate high vs decode consumption.
sre_ana: that smells like cache pressure / fragmentation. prefill workers pushing large prefixes into KV faster than decode/stream path can consume -> long stalls while waiting on KV reads + fetch retries.
oncall_jordan: customers reporting timeouts and multiple support tickets. Maya from Support flagged four enterprise customers seeing degraded UX.
support_maya: confirming — customers "BlueHorizon" and "SafeDocs" reported interactive stalls and one had 502s when streaming endpoint failed to return within timeout. They've escalated to SEs.
eng_evans: paste PromQL I'm looking at: ```
// P95 and P99 streaming latency
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(streaming_response_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, pool))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_response_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, pool))
```
infra_lee: also ran `kvcachectl dump-stats --pool us-west-1` -> top keys show large priming prefixes from a few clients; TTL pressure: avg_ttl_ms 1200, eviction_policy=lru, but fragmentation causing fragmentation_evictions: true.
sre_ana: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) throttle prefill producers (temporarily reduce prefill concurrency), 2) bump cache memory on affected pool (if spare capacity exists), 3) enable fallback routing to us-east-1 for non-low-latency customers, 4) switch some requests to smaller quantized model variant to reduce decode backlog.
oncall_jordan: agree. prioritize 1 + 4 as quick. Lee, can you reduce prefill concurrency for live prefill workers? command?
infra_lee: doing: `kubectl scale deployment/kv-prefill-workers -n inference us-west-1 --replicas=4` (was 12) -> scaling now.
sre_ana: while that scales down, I'm going to patch streaming path to prefer KV local reads with a 50ms fallback to disk rather than blocking for 500ms. small code patch rolling.
eng_evans: started canary change to fallthrough timeout: `stream.kvReadTimeout=50ms` -> applied to 2 nodes. monitoring.
support_maya: FYI customers still seeing stalls but overall fewer reports in last 4m.
incident-bot: [ACTION] runbook step applied: reduce-prefill-concurrency by oncall_jordan at 2026-03-15T09:20:12Z.
sre_ana: checking metrics: p99 down from 6-8s to ~2.2s after prefill scale down + fallthrough change. decode_queue_len_avg down to 6. eviction/sec dropped to 400. occupancy ~78%.
oncall_jordan: great. partial mitigation achieved. do we want to failover some traffic to other region for affected customers?
product_ruth: for BlueHorizon and SafeDocs we should ask before moving — they are latency sensitive, but we can propose immediate rollback to dedicated us-east nodes if they approve. contacting them now.
support_maya: sent status messages to SEs and CSMs, customers acknowledged mitigation and asked for ETA on full resolution.
infra_lee: I have a short-term config we can enable: `kvcachectl compaction --aggressive --pool us-west-1` to reduce fragmentation, but it will increase CPU for a few minutes. should we run?
sre_ana: run it sequentially on one az at a time. schedule: az-a now, az-b in 5m, az-c in 10m.
eng_evans: triggered compaction on az-a: job id comp-2369-az-a. monitoring CPU and latency.
sre_ana: post-compaction p99 back to ~1.1s on az-a. overall pool p99 trending toward 1.3s. decode queue per-node normalizing.
oncall_jordan: handoff: Ana you're primary for next 30m, I'll stay reachable but logging off shift in 15. Ana, please continue monitoring and coordinate with infra.
sre_ana: taking over. I'll keep incident open until p99 stable <1.2s for 15m.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT UPDATE] severity downgraded to high at 2026-03-15T09:30:05Z.
product_ruth: quick post-incident note: action items for postmortem — (1) tune prefill concurrency autoscaling, (2) implement prefill backpressure based on decode queue, (3) improve observability for kv fragmentation, (4) consider compaction automated trigger when fragmentation>10.
support_maya: adding customer impact notes to ticket tracker. will collect exact timestamps for each reported stall.
eng_evans: creating follow-up PR to add a token-meter to prefill path + dynamic backpressure: PR #4826.
infra_lee: created infra task to add spare capacity buffer and automated compaction job: INFRA-1298.
oncall_jordan: thanks team — solid mitigation. Final metrics: p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.2s, eviction/sec baseline back to ~120. closing paging for now.
sre_ana: will run postmortem draft and share to #postmortems in 24h.
product_ruth: thumbs up.
